job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan sat in his room, scrolling through his phone while his mother, Meena, walked in. She noticed his phone was warm and immediately asked him to put it down. Rohan laughed, saying, 'Don't worry, Ma, it's just working hard, not emitting dangerous radiation.' Meena smiled, explaining that phones use non-ionising radio waves to communicate, which are far too weak to damage human cells or make objects radioactive. She reminded him that the warmth is simply energy lost as heat during processing or charging, not a sign of harmful rays. Rohan then complained about his dry, tired eyes. Meena suggested the 20-20-20 rule, explaining that eye strain happens because we blink less while staring at screens, not because the screen shoots harmful rays into our eyes. She also pointed to his old phone on the desk, which had a slightly swollen back cover. 'That battery is a fire hazard,' she warned, 'even if it still turns on, you must stop using it immediately.' Rohan nodded, realizing that while phones are safe tools, they require responsible habits. He decided to take a break, knowing that frequent short rests are much better for his vision than one long break after hours of continuous use.

items.evidence: Meena smiled, explaining that phones use non-ionising radio waves to communicate, which are far too weak to damage human cells or make objects radioactive.
items.q: Rohan leaves a glass of water beside his phone all night. What happens to the water?
options: It stays safe, since the waves are too weak
It turns radioactive from the phone's radio waves
It becomes unsafe, as all radiation is dangerous
It soaks up radiation and passes it on
items.explain: Phone radio waves are non-ionising and far too weak to make objects radioactive.

wrong.why: thinks phones make food or water radioactive
thinks all radiation is dangerous like nuclear radiation
thinks radiation is carried and passed on afterwards

items.evidence: She reminded him that the warmth is simply energy lost as heat during processing or charging, not a sign of harmful rays.
items.q: Rohan's phone feels warm after a long game. Which is the best explanation?
options: It is losing some energy as heat while working
It is giving out dangerous rays as it heats
It is sending strong waves to a satellite
It is damaging the cells in his hand
items.explain: Warmth is just energy lost as heat during processing or charging, not harmful rays.

wrong.why: thinks a warm phone gives out dangerous radiation
thinks phones connect to a satellite for every call
thinks phone radiation damages body cells

items.evidence: Meena suggested the 20-20-20 rule, explaining that eye strain happens because we blink less while staring at screens, not because the screen shoots harmful rays into our eyes.
items.q: Why do Rohan's eyes feel dry and tired after a long time on his phone?
options: He blinks less while staring at the screen
The screen shoots harmful rays into his eyes
The screen is slowly making his eyes blind
The warm phone heats and dries his eyes
items.explain: Eye strain happens because we blink less while staring at screens, not from harmful rays.

wrong.why: believes the cause the passage rejects
links the phone's warmth to harm

items.evidence: 'That battery is a fire hazard,' she warned, 'even if it still turns on, you must stop using it immediately.'
items.q: Why did Meena tell Rohan to stop using his old phone with the swollen cover?
options: Its swollen battery could catch fire
It gives out more radiation than new phones
It no longer turns on properly
Its radio waves could damage his DNA
items.explain: A swollen battery is a fire hazard, even if the phone still turns on.

wrong.why: thinks the danger of phones is always radiation
misses that the passage says it still turns on

items.evidence: He decided to take a break, knowing that frequent short rests are much better for his vision than one long break after hours of continuous use.
items.q: Rohan must study on his phone for three hours. Which plan is best for his eyes?
options: Take short rests often during the three hours
Take one long rest after all three hours
Take no rest, since phone waves cause no effect
Take rests only when the phone feels warm
items.explain: Frequent short rests are much better for vision than one long break after hours of use.

wrong.why: reverses which kind of break is better
thinks safe waves mean screens have no effect at all
thinks warmth is the sign of harm
